Chapter 9: Forgiveness as a Path to Freedom.
You know, everyone’s been hurt by someone at some point—sometimes in those little ways that just sting, and other times in ways that leave scars that last for years. Our first instinct? Usually, it’s to hold on tight to the anger, maybe to keep ourselves safe behind walls of resentment or distance.
But here’s the thing— forgiveness isn’t about acting like nothing happened, or saying it didn’t matter. It’s about making a real choice: choosing freedom over bitterness.
Let me tell you a story. There was a man whose business partner betrayed him, left him drowning in debt and shattered trust. For months, he couldn’t stop replaying what happened, stuck in a loop of anger that felt so justified. Honestly, it probably felt necessary, like it was the only thing holding him together. But that anger? It also kept him stuck.
One day, he decided to do something different. He sat down and wrote a letter to his former partner—not to send, but just to pour out everything he’d been carrying. When he finished, he burned the letter in his backyard. The pain didn’t disappear, but somehow, its grip loosened. That’s when he realized—forgiveness is really a gift you give yourself.
Most people don’t realize just how much energy goes into holding grudges. Resentment is heavy, and if we’re not careful, it seeps into every part of our lives. It colors our relationships, and before we know it, it steals our joy. But forgiveness? It doesn’t mean you forget, or that you have to reconcile. It means you decide to let go, to stop letting what happened in the past control your present.
I remember a friend who shared her journey of forgiving her father after years of not speaking. It wasn’t quick or easy—there were setbacks, doubts, moments where she wondered if it was even possible. But with every honest conversation, every little moment of empathy, she moved a bit closer to healing. Eventually, the anger faded, and in its place was a quiet kind of peace.
Forgiveness isn’t usually something you do just once. It’s a practice—a choice you make over and over. So many people don’t even realize how much freedom is waiting for them on the other side of it. With time, forgiveness opens your heart, and suddenly, there’s space for love to grow again.
